title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Argent Financial
next_steps: Maya to send contract amendment draft for +3 regions and capacity bump
Ethan to run and share 72-hour dedicated capacity benchmark results
Share SOC2 + VPC deployment runbook with Priya
Schedule a 1-hour technical benchmark review next week
action_items: Ethan Ross: run 72-hour dedicated capacity benchmark and share results (due: 2027-04-29)
Maya Patel: send contract amendment draft for +3 regions and updated pricing (due: 2027-04-26)
Priya Desai: compile and send compliance/architecture questions for VPC deployment (due: 2027-04-25)
Lena Ortiz: confirm traffic profile and expected QPS for peak day (due: 2027-04-24)
summary: Check-in covering upcoming renewal, request for dedicated capacity expansion across additional regions, discussion of contract extension terms and compliance prerequisites for VPC/private deployment. Agreed to run a 72-hour benchmark and exchange security artifacts and a contract amendment draft.
transcript: Meeting header: 2027-04-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Recording: yes | Meeting ID: ff-20270422-argent-001
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Argent - Head of MLOps), Mohammed Khan (Argent - VP Eng), Priya Desai (Argent - Security), Samir Patel (Argent - SRE)
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: Lena here, yep
[00:12] Mohammed Khan: Mohammed, good afternoon
[00:14] Priya Desai: Priya here
[00:16] Samir Patel: Samir on the line
[00:18] Maya Patel: Great. Ethan, do you want to kick off with a quick status on usage and the capacity ask?

[00:25] Ethan Ross: Sure. Quick context: Argent's been on Redwood Hosted for the last 9 months, you moved to a pilot Dedicated pool last quarter for the fraud model, and based on the Q1 traffic profile the team is looking to expand dedicated capacity and add two more regions — EU-West and APAC — ahead of the product launch in July. This call is to align on renewal plus expansion options, and the SRE/security asks for VPC isolation if we go fuller private deployment.

[01:05] Mohammed Khan: Right, the main driver is predictable latency during peak batch scoring windows, and also we want to consolidate billing to a committed capacity contract instead of burst. We also have compliance gating the EU region for data residency, so that matters.

[01:30] Lena Ortiz: From MLOps perspective, we need the KV cache behavior to be consistent across regions; last time we saw slightly different cold-start profiles in the EU pilot. We want to run a 72-hour soak to validate steady-state p99 and token costs before we commit to full rollout.

[01:55] Ethan Ross: Totally reasonable. We can provision a Dedicated pool with the same model variants and quantization profile used in the pilot. For the soak, we'll do continuous load that mimics your peak day QPS with synthetic traffic and your real prefix caching pattern, and report latency and cost breakdowns.

[02:15] Priya Desai: On security, we need the SOC2 report and the VPC runbook — especially how PKI/KMS is integrated. We also want to know about key rotation and whether HSM is supported in the private option.

[02:38] Maya Patel: We'll share the SOC2 docs and the VPC deployment runbook after the call. Quick note: HSM integrations are supported in our Private offering and we can include KMS details in the runbook. I'll flag Ethan to coordinate with your security team during the soak.
[03:05] Samir Patel: For networking, what's the expected egress pattern? If we move to EU region with VPC, do we need to open specific ports or is it egress-only over TLS?

[03:20] Ethan Ross: It's egress outbound TLS to our control plane for metrics and rollouts. For the Private on-prem option there's an optional air-gapped mode, but for VPC we'll list required egress endpoints. We'll include firewall rules (IP ranges + FQDNs) in the runbook.
[03:45] Mohammed Khan: Pricing — we were quoted committed capacity pricing last quarter, what's the delta if we add 50% more GPUs and two regions? We need an estimate to take to procurement.

[03:58] Maya Patel: I'll put together an amendment with committed capacity tiers. High level: the per-GPU committed unit price reduces with a 12-month term; adding regions incurs a small regional replication fee. I'll include an example with +50% capacity and EU/APAC extras. Expect a draft by Monday.
[04:25] Lena Ortiz: On the benchmark: can we also collect token-level cost breakdowns and per-model tail latencies? Those metrics will determine if we need model variant fallbacks in some regions.

[04:40] Ethan Ross: Yes, we'll include token-level cost, per-model p50/p95/p99, and KV cache hit/miss rates. Also we'll surface automatic fallback behavior if capacity is constrained — e.g., route to hosted variants with slightly higher latency but lower cost.

[05:05] Priya Desai: Regarding data retention — in the hosted flow you log some telemetry. If we move to Dedicated with VPC, can you confirm log retention windows and whether logs containing PII can be disabled?

[05:20] Maya Patel: We can disable application-level telemetry that contains PII and we support configurable retention windows. For Private deployments customers can keep control plane logs within their VPC and we provide an option to route logs to your Kinesis/Splunk.
[05:42] Mohammed Khan: There's also a procurement timeline — ideally we want the contract signed by mid-May to align budget cycles. Is that feasible if we run the soak this week?
[05:55] Maya Patel: If the soak finishes and results look good, yes. That's why the 72-hour benchmark and timely artifacts are important.
[06:10] Ethan Ross: Operational note: we'll need an access window to run the synthetic traffic and coordinate with Samir for IP allowlisting. Can we lock that in now?
[06:20] Samir Patel: We can allowlist a CIDR block for the soak, but I'd prefer a scheduled window so we can monitor and rollback policies if needed. Week of April 26 works for us.

[06:35] Maya Patel: Great — so plan: Ethan runs 72-hour soak starting April 26, shares results April 29. Maya shares contract amendment and pricing April 26. Priya and team will receive SOC2 and VPC runbook today and follow up with security questions by April 25.

[06:55] Lena Ortiz: Small technical question — during the pilot we saw a KV cache eviction rate spike when sequence lengths increased. Is there a tuning we should apply across regions to match the production workload?

[07:10] Ethan Ross: We can tune cache partitions and warm prefixes. Also switching to a slightly larger KV shard size for the dedicated hosts helped another customer with similar patterns. We'll include recommended config in the soak plan and run a couple of A/Bs.
[07:35] Mohammed Khan: On rollback policies — if we do canary rollout of the new region, what is the automatic fallback? Does traffic route to hosted Redwood or to our other dedicated pools?

[07:50] Ethan Ross: The default canary is to keep a percentage on the new region; if p99 breaches the threshold it automatically routes to your other Dedicated pool or to a hosted-compatible variant based on your policy. We'll share the exact routing policy JSON in the runbook.
[08:10] Priya Desai: For compliance we need audit logs that show model version, who invoked the API, and payload hashes. Do you support that level of audit?

[08:23] Maya Patel: Yes, audit logs include model versions, request metadata, and actions. Payload hashing is supported; full payload capture can be disabled. We'll include a sample audit log and retention options in the package.
[08:45] Samir Patel: Network performance question: is cross-region replication synchronous for config and cache? We want to avoid cross-region latency in the hot path.

[09:00] Ethan Ross: Config replication is near real-time via our control plane. KV cache isn't replicated cross-region — the cache is local to the Dedicated pool to avoid cross-region latency; we rely on prefix warming to mitigate cold starts.
[09:20] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. One more ask — support for a scheduled auto-scale window during marketing spikes. Does Redwood Dedicated support scheduled scale-ups?
[09:33] Ethan Ross: Yes, you can define scheduled scaling policies as well as load-based autoscaling. There is also a burst capacity option if you need short term headroom.
[09:45] Mohammed Khan: From procurement side, are there termination clauses for overprovisioning? We want to avoid multi-month penalties if we misestimate capacity.

[09:58] Maya Patel: Standard committed capacity contracts include a right-sizing review at the 3-month mark. We can build in a one-time true-up adjustment to avoid large penalties; I'll include flexible options in the amendment.
[10:20] — (brief sidebar: Maya and Mohammed exchange calendar invites; audio overlaps slightly) —

[11:00] Ethan Ross: Ok I want to call out two technical risks: 1) quantization differences across GPU types that could slightly change llm outputs — we'll surface quality regression metrics during the soak; 2) prefix cache warm-up time for cold starts — we'll measure token cost impact.
[11:30] Lena Ortiz: On quality regressions — we need to lock-down baseline evals before cutover. Can you accept a short eval suite?
[11:40] Ethan Ross: Absolutely, send a small eval set and we'll run the regressions as part of the soak and include alerts if quality drops beyond the threshold.
[12:00] Priya Desai: Also, encryption-at-rest — does Redwood support customer-managed keys (CMK) for model artifacts and KV cache?
[12:12] Maya Patel: Yes, CMKs supported in Private and in Dedicated with optional KMS integration. We'll note HSM availability for on-prem.
[12:30] Mohammed Khan: If everything checks out, what's the lead time to spin up two additional Dedicated pools in EU and APAC?

[12:40] Ethan Ross: Typical lead time is 2-3 weeks once capacity is committed and networking is cleared. For urgent cases we can prioritize and often do it in 10 business days if the regions have available capacity.
[13:00] Lena Ortiz: Can you give an estimated per-token cost delta if we move from hosted to dedicated with our current model and quantization? We need rough unit economics to compare.

[13:12] Ethan Ross: Rough ballpark: dedicated with committed units tends to be 25-40% cheaper per token depending on batch efficiency and cache hit rate. We'll provide a model-specific estimate in the amendment doc.
[13:35] Maya Patel: I'll include both a 12-month and 24-month committed pricing scenario so procurement can evaluate tradeoffs.
[13:50] Samir Patel: Operationally, who is our on-call if there's an incident in the new regions? We need SLAs and an incident contact list.
[14:00] Maya Patel: Dedicated customers get a named CSM and an on-call engineering rotation for Sev1. We'll include contact lists and SLAs in the contract pack.
[14:20] Mohammed Khan: Let's talk timeline recap: we want contract signed mid-May, soak finished by Apr 29, and next week do a deep technical review. Is that aligned?
[14:33] Maya Patel: Yes. Action items as stated earlier. I'll also propose two slots next week for a 60-minute benchmark review and a contract discussion.
[15:00] Lena Ortiz: One last technical nit — replication of model weights for region spin-ups; can we pre-stage weights so the first inference isn't blocked by download?
[15:12] Ethan Ross: Yes, we can pre-stage model artifacts on the Dedicated nodes as part of provisioning. We'll coordinate with your SRE for the content hash verification.
[15:30] — (brief silence, people review slide link Maya shared in chat) —

[16:00] Maya Patel: Ok I'll read back the next steps: 1) Ethan runs 72-hour soak starting April 26 and shares results April 29; 2) Maya sends contract amendment with region add and pricing by April 26; 3) Redwood sends SOC2 and VPC runbook today; 4) Priya sends security questions by April 25; 5) schedule 1-hour benchmark review next week. Anything missing?
[16:30] Priya Desai: That's good from security side.
[16:32] Mohammed Khan: Sounds good.
[16:35] Lena Ortiz: Good summary. We'll confirm the soak window and provide the peak QPS profile by April 24.
[16:45] Maya Patel: Awesome, thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the artifacts. Talk soon.
[16:52] (meeting ends)
References/links shared in chat: SOC2_report_v3.pdf (link), VPC_runbook_draft.docx (link), pricing_example_draft.xlsx (link)
